soils.name: Airy houseplant mix
soils.short: good universal potting mix with extra perlite
soils.note: Squeeze a handful when moist: it should hold together and then crumble.

soils.name: Chunky aroid mix
soils.short: chunky aroid mix (bark, perlite, coco coir)
soils.note: Their roots climb trees in the wild, so they want air as much as water.

soils.name: Gritty succulent mix
soils.note: Water should run straight through. If the mix stays dark for more than a few days, add more grit.

soils.name: Orchid bark mix
soils.note: Air-loving roots: no ordinary compost at all.

soils.name: Ericaceous mix
soils.note: Buy bags labelled ericaceous or lime-free, and water with rainwater where you can.

soils.name: Veg and herb compost
soils.note: Rich and moisture-holding, for hungry fast growers.

soils.name: Moisture-keeping mix
soils.note: Stays evenly damp without going soggy.

soils.name: Mediterranean mix
soils.note: Lean and sunny: rich compost makes them soft and short-lived.

soils.name: African violet mix
soils.note: Very light and fluffy so fine roots can spread.

soils.name: Carnivorous plant mix
soils.short: carnivorous plant mix (sphagnum peat and sand, no fertilizer)
soils.note: Nutrient-free on purpose. Rainwater or distilled water only.

soils.name: No soil
soils.short: no soil at all (mounted or loose)

components.name: Perlite
components.note: Puffed volcanic glass. Light, doesn't break down, keeps roots breathing.

components.name: Pumice
components.note: Porous volcanic stone. Heavier than perlite, so it stays mixed in and steadies tall pots.

components.name: Orchid bark
components.note: Fir or pine bark pieces. Big gaps for air, slowly breaks down over 1–2 years.

components.name: Coco coir
components.note: Coconut husk fibre. A peat-free sponge that rewets easily. Rinse salty brands first.

components.name: Peat-free compost
components.note: Wood fibre, green compost and coir. Holds moisture and some food; kinder to bogs.

components.name: Sphagnum peat
components.note: Only for plants that truly need it, like carnivorous plants. Use sparingly.

components.name: Sphagnum moss
components.note: Living or dried moss. Great for rooting cuttings and orchids.

components.name: Horticultural grit
components.note: Small washed stones. Makes mixes heavy and fast-draining for succulents and herbs.

components.name: Coarse sand
components.note: Sharp, washed sand only. Fine play sand clogs pores.

components.name: Horticultural charcoal
components.note: Light chunks that add air. Doesn't purify water, but helps the mix stay open.

components.name: Worm castings
components.note: A mild, slow natural food. 10% is plenty.

components.name: Akadama
components.note: Baked Japanese clay granules. Loved by bonsai growers; breaks down after a few years.

components.name: Vermiculite
components.note: Expanded mineral flakes. Good for seeds and moisture lovers.

components.name: LECA clay balls
components.note: Expanded clay pebbles. Used on their own for semi-hydro growing or as a chunky additive.

fertilizers.name: Balanced liquid feed
fertilizers.cadence: Every 4 weeks, spring to early autumn
fertilizers.dilution: Half to full label strength, on moist soil
fertilizers.rest: Pause from mid-autumn to early spring

fertilizers.name: Gentle liquid feed
fertilizers.cadence: Every 4–6 weeks in the growing season
fertilizers.note: For slow growers and plants that burn easily.

fertilizers.name: Cactus & succulent feed
fertilizers.rest: No food at all from October to March
fertilizers.note: Too much nitrogen makes them soft and floppy.

fertilizers.name: Orchid feed
fertilizers.dilution: Quarter strength, and flush with plain water monthly
fertilizers.rest: Reduce in winter, pause while resting
fertilizers.note: Weak and often: their roots are sensitive to salts.

fertilizers.name: Ericaceous feed
fertilizers.cadence: Every 4 weeks from spring to late summer
fertilizers.rest: Stop in late summer so wood can ripen
fertilizers.note: Keeps leaves green on lime-hating plants.

fertilizers.name: Citrus feed
fertilizers.cadence: Every 2–3 weeks in summer, monthly in winter
fertilizers.rest: Lighter but not zero in winter
fertilizers.note: Includes iron, magnesium and zinc that citrus crave.

fertilizers.name: Flower & fruit feed
fertilizers.rest: Pause once flowering and fruiting stop

fertilizers.name: Foliar feed
fertilizers.cadence: Monthly, misted or added to soaking water
fertilizers.note: For air plants and bromeliads that drink through leaves.

fertilizers.name: No fertilizer
fertilizers.cadence: Never: they catch their own food

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.signs: Fine webbing, dusty speckled leaves, tiny moving dots underneath.
pests.fix: Shower the plant well, wipe leaves, raise humidity, and repeat every 5 days for three weeks. Insecticidal soap for stubborn cases.

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.signs: White cottony tufts in leaf joints and under leaves, sticky residue.
pests.fix: Dab each tuft with a cotton bud dipped in rubbing alcohol, then check weekly. Isolate until clear.

pests.name: Root mealybugs
pests.signs: White waxy patches on roots and inside the pot, plant stalls.
pests.fix: Unpot, wash the roots clean, discard old soil and repot into a fresh mix and clean pot.

pests.name: Scale insects
pests.signs: Small brown or tan bumps on stems and leaf veins, sticky leaves.
pests.fix: Scrape off gently with a fingernail or soft brush, wipe with soapy water, recheck every week.

pests.name: Fungus gnats
pests.signs: Tiny black flies hovering around the soil.
pests.fix: Let the top of the soil dry out, use yellow sticky traps, and water from below for a few weeks.

pests.name: Thrips
pests.signs: Silvery streaks, black specks and twisted new leaves.
pests.fix: Shower the plant, use blue sticky traps and wipe leaves with insecticidal soap weekly.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.signs: Clusters of small green, black or pink insects on tips and buds.
pests.fix: Squash or rinse them off with water. Ladybirds and lacewings help outdoors.

pests.name: Whitefly
pests.signs: Clouds of tiny white flies rising when you brush the leaves.
pests.fix: Yellow sticky traps, and rinse leaf undersides every few days.
pests.likes: Warm, still air, tomatoes and herbs

pests.name: Cyclamen mites
pests.fix: Hard to clear: remove damaged growth and isolate. Discard badly hit plants.

pests.name: Vine weevil
pests.signs: Notched leaf edges above, plant collapsing as grubs eat roots below.
pests.fix: Check the root ball for C-shaped grubs. Nematodes watered in late summer work well.

pests.name: Slugs and snails
pests.fix: Night-time hand picking, copper tape on pots, and wildlife-friendly traps.

pests.name: Bulb flies
pests.signs: Grassy, flowerless leaves from soft bulbs.
pests.fix: Firm, healthy bulbs only; plant deep and mulch.
